articles.title: Create your first wallet
articles.summary: Start with a new wallet, then give it a name and color you recognize.
articles.body: Getting started Create your first wallet Start with a new wallet, then give it a name and color you recognize. Oath 4.0.3 Where to find it Welcome → Create a new wallet How to do it On Welcome, choose Create a new wallet. To restore an existing wallet instead, choose Import wallet or Restore from iCloud. Create a six-digit app passcode and enter it again to confirm. Complete biometric setup if offered and desired. On Customize Wallet, enter a recognizable name and choose a color. Tap Continue to open the wallet. Check the wallet name on Home, then open Receive for the network you intend to use. Do not fund an example address from a help screenshot. Open the wallet’s settings and make a recovery backup before receiving funds. Keep the recovery phrase and any passphrase separately from the phone. Return to Home and allow balances and activity to refresh. A brand-new wallet can correctly show no activity and zero balances. A newly created recovery-phrase wallet has new keys and addresses. Choosing a familiar name does not restore an older wallet; use Import or Restore for that. Keep the recovery phrase and any additional passphrase independently of the app passcode. Before funding, verify that you have a usable recovery route. Verify the wallet name and intended public address after setup. A newly generated wallet and an imported wallet can have the same label while controlling different accounts. Follow along in Oath Real app screens with illustrative demo data. No live funds were sent, swapped or revoked for these examples. Never send funds to an example address. Tap an image to inspect it at full size. 1 Choose creation for a new wallet, import for an existing phrase, or More Options for other supported recovery routes. See step 1 . 2 Enter and confirm your own app passcode privately. The screenshot shows an empty setup screen, not a usable passcode. 3 Choose a recognizable name and color, then Continue to finish setup. This is an example wallet, not a recovered account. Good to know A new wallet is different from importing an existing one. Your app passcode unlocks Oath; it is not a recovery phrase or backup password.

articles.title: Import a recovery phrase
articles.summary: Bring an existing wallet into Oath using its BIP-39 recovery words.
articles.body: Getting started Import a recovery phrase Bring an existing wallet into Oath using its BIP-39 recovery words. Oath 4.0.3 Where to find it Welcome → Import wallet How to do it Tap Import wallet. If you already use Oath, open Settings → Wallets → Import wallet. Enter the words in their original order, use Paste, or use the scan button for a compatible recovery QR. Review any word-count, unknown-word or checksum message. Correct the original phrase rather than guessing new words. Tap Import. On first setup, create and confirm your app passcode. Name and customize the wallet, then tap Continue. After import, open Receive on the original network and compare the full public address with your previous wallet. Use a supported address/path choice if the original account requires it. Wait for balances and history to refresh. If an address differs, check recovery language, word order, additional passphrase and supported account rules; importing a valid phrase alone does not prove it is the intended account. Import reconstructs supported accounts from the phrase; it does not move coins on-chain. Enter the original order and language, and never replace an invalid word by guessing. A separate BIP-39 passphrase creates different accounts. If your previous wallet used one, restore that exact passphrase wallet and compare addresses before concluding a balance is missing. Verify the wallet name and intended public address after setup. A newly generated wallet and an imported wallet can have the same label while controlling different accounts. Follow along in Oath Real app screens with illustrative demo data. No live funds were sent, swapped or revoked for these examples. Never send funds to an example address. Tap an image to inspect it at full size. 1 Enter words privately in their original order, or use Paste or the scan control. Recovery words are deliberately absent from all screenshots. See step 1 . 2 Choose a recognizable name and color, then Continue to finish setup. This is an example wallet, not a recovered account. Good to know Never enter recovery words into this website, a support message, or an online checker. A wallet protected by a BIP-39 passphrase also needs that exact passphrase.

articles.title: Scan a recovery-phrase QR code
articles.summary: Use the camera to import a compatible recovery phrase without typing every word.
articles.body: Getting started Scan a recovery-phrase QR code Use the camera to import a compatible recovery phrase without typing every word. Oath 4.0.3 Where to find it Import wallet → scan icon How to do it Open Import wallet and tap the scan icon in the navigation bar. Allow camera access when iOS asks. Point the camera at a recovery QR you trust. After a recognized phrase fills the field, review validation and tap Import. If camera access was denied, use Open Settings in the error message, enable Camera for Oath and try again. A recovery QR contains secret material. Scan it privately from a source you control, not from a public website or a person offering support. The import validation still applies after scanning. A recognized QR is not proof that the wallet belongs to you or has a trustworthy history. Verify the wallet name and intended public address after setup. A newly generated wallet and an imported wallet can have the same label while controlling different accounts. Follow along in Oath Real app screens with illustrative demo data. No live funds were sent, swapped or revoked for these examples. Never send funds to an example address. Tap an image to inspect it at full size. 1 Enter words privately in their original order, or use Paste or the scan control. Recovery words are deliberately absent from all screenshots. See step 1 . 2 Use a recognizable local name and color, then finish with the displayed confirmation control. Good to know A receiving-address QR is not a recovery phrase. Do not share or photograph recovery QR codes.

articles.title: Import a private key
articles.summary: Import the key for a particular network or the shared Ethereum & EVM group.
articles.body: Getting started Import a private key Import the key for a particular network or the shared Ethereum & EVM group. Oath 4.0.3 Where to find it Welcome → more options → Import private key How to do it Open Import private key from the welcome options or Settings → Wallets. Choose the network. Ethereum & EVM groups the supported EVM networks into one import choice. Enter or paste the private key in the format expected by that network. Review the validation result. Confirm the import, complete first-time passcode setup if asked, then customize the wallet. Open Receive for the chosen network and compare the full address with the original account. Do not rely only on its nickname or logo. Keep the original key or a verified encrypted backup. Allow fresh network data to load; importing does not transfer any funds on-chain. A private-key wallet usually restores one key or a supported scoped account, not all accounts generated by a recovery phrase. Choose the import type that matches your original recovery material. Review the address after import. A valid key in the wrong network or derivation context can show an account you did not intend. Verify the wallet name and intended public address after setup. A newly generated wallet and an imported wallet can have the same label while controlling different accounts. Follow along in Oath Real app screens with illustrative demo data. No live funds were sent, swapped or revoked for these examples. Never send funds to an example address. Tap an image to inspect it at full size. 1 Choose the network that matches the original key export before entering any key. See step 1 . 2 The import form validates the format for the selected network. No private-key value is shown. Good to know A private-key wallet does not have a recovery phrase in Oath. Keep the original key or an encrypted backup. A single private key and an extended HD key are not the same kind of recovery material.

articles.title: Which private-key formats can I import?
articles.summary: Choose the correct network before entering key material. Oath validates both format and key structure.
articles.body: Getting started Which private-key formats can I import? Choose the correct network before entering key material. Oath validates both format and key structure. Oath 4.0.3 Where to find it Settings → Wallets → Import private key How to do it For Bitcoin-family networks, use the supported WIF, raw key or extended private-key form for that network. An account-scoped extended key only recovers the addresses within its scope. For Ethereum & EVM or TRON, use a 32-byte hexadecimal key. Solana accepts its Base58 keypair or a JSON byte-array keypair. NEAR expects an ed25519: keypair; Stellar uses an S-prefixed secret StrKey. Sui uses an Ed25519 suiprivkey value. Aptos accepts an Ed25519 hexadecimal or AIP-80 key. XRP Ledger uses a supported secp256k1 key; Gram uses a supported Ed25519 hexadecimal key. Do not convert formats by manually trimming characters or discarding bytes. Use the original supported export and correct network choice. If Oath rejects a format, stop and identify the original wallet’s export type. A public address, extended public key or keystore password alone is not a private key. Verify the wallet name and intended public address after setup. A newly generated wallet and an imported wallet can have the same label while controlling different accounts. Follow along in Oath Real app screens with illustrative demo data. No live funds were sent, swapped or revoked for these examples. Never send funds to an example address. Tap an image to inspect it at full size. 1 Choose the network that matches the original key export before entering any key. See step 1 . 2 The import form validates the format for the selected network. No private-key value is shown. Good to know Do not convert keys on an unfamiliar website. A public address, xpub, or transaction ID is not a private key. Other signature schemes or wallet-specific export formats may not import.

If biometric authentication is available, complete the Face ID or Touch ID prompt to enable it. Continue to wallet customization. Keep your recovery backup independently of this passcode. The six-digit app passcode protects local wallet access; it is not the recovery phrase or your iCloud backup password. Keep all three roles separate. Losing the phone can require recovery material even when you remember the app passcode. Verify the wallet name and intended public address after setup. A newly generated wallet and an imported wallet can have the same label while controlling different accounts. Follow along in Oath Real app screens with illustrative demo data. No live funds were sent, swapped or revoked for these examples. Never send funds to an example address. Tap an image to inspect it at full size. 1 Choose creation for a new wallet, import for an existing phrase, or More Options for other supported recovery routes. See step 1 . 2 Enter and confirm your own app passcode privately. The screenshot shows an empty setup screen, not a usable passcode. 3 Use a recognizable local name and color, then finish with the displayed confirmation control. articles.title: Find your way around Home
articles.summary: Use the Wallet, History and Search icons, and find the controls for your active wallet.
articles.body: Getting started Find your way around Home Use the Wallet, History and Search icons, and find the controls for your active wallet. Oath 4.0.3 Where to find it Bottom navigation → Wallet How to do it Open the Wallet tab to see the active wallet’s total and Assets list. Use the wallet-name capsule in the top toolbar to switch wallets. The adjacent sliders action opens Settings; the scanner opens the shared QR scanner. Read the balance-change capsule under the total as an observed change in this wallet’s value. It is not a profit report or a button for a balance-history chart. Tap Send or Receive for a transfer flow. Tap an asset for its price, actions and activity. Select Wallet and then the separate Search icon to search assets, including an exact contract or mint address. Open History for transactions across the active wallet. Pull down from the top to refresh; cached information can remain visible while newer data arrives. Wallet, History and Search are different views of the same active wallet. Selecting the Wallet navigation icon returns to Home. The name capsule in the top toolbar opens the wallet switcher. Search follows the last section you selected: Wallet searches assets, while History searches transactions. Select the section you want before opening Search. For the main Settings screen, return to the top of Home until the sliders icon is visible. Currency, Language and Appearance are directly in Settings; there is no separate Preferences screen. A long wallet name stays on one line and ends with an ellipsis inside the capsule. VoiceOver reads the full name. The wallet’s saved name is not shortened or changed. Follow along in Oath Real app screens with illustrative demo data. No live funds were sent, swapped or revoked for these examples. Never send funds to an example address. Tap an image to inspect it at full size. 1 Check the active wallet in the toolbar, then use Send, Receive, asset filters or the bottom History and Search controls. Balances are illustrative. See step 1 . 2 Names, colors, balances and the active badge distinguish wallets. Choose the intended wallet before starting an action. Good to know The total is a valuation based on available balances, prices and exchange rates. Missing or delayed provider data can affect it. Check the actual asset quantity and network when reviewing a transfer.

articles.title: Add another wallet
articles.summary: Keep separate wallets in the same app without replacing the one you already use.
articles.body: Your wallets Add another wallet Keep separate wallets in the same app without replacing the one you already use. Oath 4.0.3 Where to find it Home → wallet-name capsule in the top toolbar → add-wallet action How to do it Tap the wallet-name capsule in the top toolbar on Home to open the switcher. Settings → Wallets also offers the add-wallet actions. Choose Create a new wallet, Import wallet, Import private key or Restore from iCloud. Complete that flow and choose a name and color you can recognize. When setup finishes, check the wallet name on Home and the active check badge in the switcher. Verify the receiving address before using the wallet. The list also shows a local-currency value for each wallet when a saved valuation is available. These are separate wallets, even when they share the same app passcode. Return to Wallets and confirm the intended wallet and active selection. A local management action does not itself transfer funds or change network permissions. After adding, confirm the active wallet in Home’s toolbar before sending or sharing a receiving address. A wallet list can contain similar names with different keys. Follow along in Oath Real app screens with illustrative demo data. No live funds were sent, swapped or revoked for these examples. Never send funds to an example address. Tap an image to inspect it at full size. 1 Check the active wallet in the toolbar, then use Send, Receive, asset filters or the bottom History and Search controls. Balances are illustrative. See step 1 . 2 Names, colors, balances and the active badge distinguish wallets. Choose the intended wallet before starting an action. Good to know Additional wallets share the app lock. They remain separate wallet records; adding a wallet does not transfer funds.

articles.title: Switch wallets from Home
articles.summary: Use the glass name capsule above your balance to select another wallet or add one.
articles.body: Your wallets Switch wallets from Home Use the glass name capsule above your balance to select another wallet or add one. Oath 4.0.3 Where to find it Wallet → wallet-name capsule above the balance How to do it Return to Home and tap the wallet-name capsule in the top toolbar. Find the intended wallet by name and color. The check badge marks the active wallet. Tap its row and wait for Home to load that wallet. Read the name in the toolbar before continuing. Open Receive and compare the public address for the intended network, especially when two wallets have similar names. To add another wallet, use the create, import, private-key import or iCloud restore actions in the switcher or Settings → Wallets. The name capsule and balance are separate buttons. Tapping the capsule opens the switcher; tapping the large amount hides or reveals balances. Long names are shortened visually with an ellipsis so the capsule remains on one line. Open the switcher to identify the wallet, or use VoiceOver to hear the complete name. The saved wallet name is unchanged. Switching changes the active wallet used by Home and History. Asset navigation, searches and history filters reset for the newly selected wallet so they do not keep showing results from the previous one. Creating or importing a wallet continues through the existing setup and customization flow. Phrase and private-key import open after the switcher closes. Restore from iCloud opens its backup list in the sheet. Use the sliders icon for app settings and the wallet-colored toolbar shortcut after scrolling for current-wallet settings. Settings → Wallets still opens management; its rows are separate from the Home switcher. Follow along in Oath Real app screens with illustrative demo data. No live funds were sent, swapped or revoked for these examples. Never send funds to an example address. Tap an image to inspect it at full size. 1 Names, colors, balances and the active badge distinguish wallets. Choose the intended wallet before starting an action. See step 1 . 2 Check the active wallet in the toolbar, then use Send, Receive, asset filters or the bottom History and Search controls. Balances are illustrative. Good to know Switching wallets does not transfer funds. A wallet-row valuation can use cached balances and prices; it is not a guarantee of a fresh network check.

articles.title: Change a wallet’s name and color
articles.summary: Give each wallet a visual identity that is easy to recognize.
articles.body: Your wallets Change a wallet’s name and color Give each wallet a visual identity that is easy to recognize. Oath 4.0.3 Where to find it Settings → Wallets → wallet → Customize Wallet How to do it Open the wallet you want to customize. Tap Customize Wallet and edit its name. Choose a preset color or open the color picker. Tap Apply. When creating, importing or restoring a wallet, the same action is labeled Continue. A wallet name and color are local labels that help you distinguish accounts. Editing them does not change the wallet’s blockchain addresses. Use names that remain clear in the switcher and transaction review. Check the active wallet after returning Home. Return to Wallets and confirm the intended wallet and active selection. A local management action does not itself transfer funds or change network permissions. Follow along in Oath Real app screens with illustrative demo data. No live funds were sent, swapped or revoked for these examples. Never send funds to an example address. Tap an image to inspect it at full size. 1 Use a recognizable local name and color, then finish with the displayed confirmation control. See step 1 . 2 Check the wallet name before choosing customization, recovery, private-key, backup or removal actions. Good to know The color changes the wallet artwork. Appearance mode and the app icon are controlled separately under Settings → Appearance.

articles.title: Reorder your wallets
articles.summary: Put frequently used wallets where you want them in the list.
articles.body: Your wallets Reorder your wallets Put frequently used wallets where you want them in the list. Oath 4.0.3 Where to find it Settings → Wallets → Edit How to do it Open Settings → Wallets and tap Edit. Drag a wallet by its reorder handle to the position you want. Repeat as needed, then tap the native checkmark in the top bar to finish editing. Reopen Wallets to see the saved order. The check badge on a wallet icon still identifies the active wallet. The checkmark in the top bar is an action that finishes editing. The small check attached to a wallet’s icon is a selection badge; it is not a second Done button. Reordering changes the wallet list only. It does not change the order of assets or move funds between wallets. Reordering changes the list order, not the active wallet or its keys. The check badge identifies selection independently of position. Use the native editing handles and finish with the toolbar checkmark so the list exits editing mode. Follow along in Oath Real app screens with illustrative demo data. No live funds were sent, swapped or revoked for these examples. Never send funds to an example address. Tap an image to inspect it at full size. 1 Names, colors, balances and the active badge distinguish wallets. Choose the intended wallet before starting an action. See step 1 . 2 Check the wallet name before choosing customization, recovery, private-key, backup or removal actions. Good to know This changes wallet order. Asset lists are sorted by portfolio value and activity, not by this setting.

articles.title: Move a wallet to Recently Deleted
articles.summary: Remove a wallet from the active list while keeping a short recovery window.
articles.body: Your wallets Move a wallet to Recently Deleted Remove a wallet from the active list while keeping a short recovery window. Oath 4.0.3 Where to find it Settings → Wallets → Edit How to do it Tap Edit and use the remove control for the wallet. Authenticate with enabled biometrics or your app passcode when requested. Read the native confirmation dialog and confirm removal. Find the removed wallet under Recently Deleted in the Wallets screen. For an ordinary removal while other active wallets remain, the wallet enters Recently Deleted for seven days. This affects the local app, not funds or token approvals on the blockchain. Removing the final active wallet instead follows a reset flow. If Recently Deleted contains wallets, Oath asks you to permanently remove those first. Cancel if you do not have recovery material for them. After the final active wallet is removed, Oath returns to Welcome. Existing iCloud files are separate from the local deletion; protect their passwords and remove cloud copies separately only if that is your intention. Follow along in Oath Real app screens with illustrative demo data. No live funds were sent, swapped or revoked for these examples. Never send funds to an example address. Tap an image to inspect it at full size. 1 Names, colors, balances and the active badge distinguish wallets. Choose the intended wallet before starting an action. See step 1 . 2 Read the deletion deadline. Restore returns retained wallets; Delete Permanently closes this local recovery route after confirmation. Good to know Removed wallets are retained for seven days before automatic cleanup. Removing a wallet does not move on-chain funds or delete an existing iCloud backup. Keep a separate backup before removal.

articles.title: Recover a recently deleted wallet
articles.summary: Bring a wallet back before its retention window expires.
articles.body: Your wallets Recover a recently deleted wallet Bring a wallet back before its retention window expires. Oath 4.0.3 Where to find it Settings → Wallets → Recently Deleted How to do it Open Settings → Wallets → Recently Deleted before the displayed deletion deadline. Select the wallets to restore. Use Select All or Deselect All to change the selection. Tap Restore. Complete authentication if requested and wait for the operation to finish. Return to Wallets, choose the restored wallet and check its receiving address and refreshed assets. Removed wallets normally remain recoverable locally for seven days. Each row shows its own deadline; expired items are permanently removed the next time Oath is unlocked. Restore returns the retained wallet to the active list. If it was permanently deleted, use its original recovery material or encrypted iCloud backup instead. Removing the final active wallet is a different flow: it requires clearing Recently Deleted and then resets the local app. Follow along in Oath Real app screens with illustrative demo data. No live funds were sent, swapped or revoked for these examples. Never send funds to an example address. Tap an image to inspect it at full size. 1 Read the deletion deadline. Restore returns retained wallets; Delete Permanently closes this local recovery route after confirmation. See step 1 . 2 Names, colors, balances and the active badge distinguish wallets. Choose the intended wallet before starting an action. Good to know Each row shows when removal becomes permanent. Do not rely on Recently Deleted as your only backup.

articles.title: Permanently delete removed wallets
articles.summary: Clear wallets from Recently Deleted when you no longer need their local copies.
articles.body: Your wallets Permanently delete removed wallets Clear wallets from Recently Deleted when you no longer need their local copies. Oath 4.0.3 Where to find it Settings → Wallets → Recently Deleted How to do it Open Recently Deleted and select the wallets you intend to erase. Compare their names and deletion dates. Check that you have an independently usable recovery phrase, private key or encrypted backup for anything you may need later. Tap Delete Permanently, the destructive secondary button below Restore. Read the confirmation and authenticate if requested. Confirm only the selected wallets you intend to erase. After completion, verify those rows are gone. A permanently deleted wallet cannot be restored from Recently Deleted. Return to Wallets and confirm the intended wallet and active selection. A local management action does not itself transfer funds or change network permissions. The displayed deletion deadline is a remaining local recovery window, not a blockchain expiry. Permanent deletion closes that local recovery route immediately. Read the selected count and names again at confirmation. If you are uncertain about a backup, cancel and restore the wallet first so you can verify its recovery options. Follow along in Oath Real app screens with illustrative demo data. No live funds were sent, swapped or revoked for these examples. Never send funds to an example address. Tap an image to inspect it at full size. 1 Read the deletion deadline. Restore returns retained wallets; Delete Permanently closes this local recovery route after confirmation. See step 1 . Good to know Permanent deletion cannot be undone using Recently Deleted. Existing external backups and on-chain records are separate.

articles.title: Create a wallet with a BIP-39 passphrase
articles.summary: Derive a separate wallet from the same recovery phrase plus an exact passphrase.
articles.body: Your wallets Create a wallet with a BIP-39 passphrase Derive a separate wallet from the same recovery phrase plus an exact passphrase. Oath 4.0.3 Where to find it Settings → Wallets → wallet → Add Passphrase How to do it Choose a recovery-phrase wallet and tap Add Passphrase. Read the explanation and continue. Enter the passphrase and its confirmation exactly, including capitalization and spaces. Use the eye control to check your entry privately. Create the wallet, then choose its name and color. Back up the new passphrase wallet too. The additional BIP-39 passphrase is part of the key derivation. Every different value, including differences in case or spaces, produces a different wallet. It is not the app passcode and not an iCloud encryption password. Record the exact phrase and passphrase together in a secure recovery plan; the passphrase wallet needs its own verification and backup. Return to Wallets and confirm the intended wallet and active selection. A local management action does not itself transfer funds or change network permissions. Follow along in Oath Real app screens with illustrative demo data. No live funds were sent, swapped or revoked for these examples. Never send funds to an example address. Tap an image to inspect it at full size. 1 Select the appropriate recovery-phrase wallet before creating its passphrase-derived wallet. See step 1 . 2 The additional passphrase changes the derived wallet. Enter the exact value privately and keep it with your recovery plan. Good to know This does not add a password to the existing wallet. Every different passphrase produces a different wallet; you need both the recovery phrase and that exact passphrase to recover it. The option is not available for private-key wallets.

articles.title: Back up all wallets to iCloud
articles.summary: Start an encrypted backup for every active wallet from one screen.
articles.body: Backup & recovery Back up all wallets to iCloud Start an encrypted backup for every active wallet from one screen. Oath 4.0.3 Where to find it Settings → Backup How to do it Tap Back Up All Wallets. Choose a backup password of at least eight characters and confirm it. Keep it somewhere safe. Tap Back Up and keep Oath open while it prepares the encrypted wallet files. Check every wallet’s status. Preparation or uploading is not the same as a completed backup. The backup flow encrypts the supported wallet material before saving backup files to your iCloud Drive. The backup password is required to restore those files. Check each wallet’s outcome. A batch can contain a failed upload even when another wallet completed; retain an independent recovery copy until the relevant upload is confirmed. Treat the backup as usable only when the relevant operation has completed and you retain the correct recovery material or file password. Loading, preparing and unavailable states are not successful backups. Follow along in Oath Real app screens with illustrative demo data. No live funds were sent, swapped or revoked for these examples. Never send funds to an example address. Tap an image to inspect it at full size. 1 This simulator has no iCloud account, so it shows the real unavailable state. This is not a completed backup; use an eligible signed-in device to upload. See step 1 . 2 Set and confirm the password for the encrypted backup. Empty fields are shown deliberately; the screenshot does not demonstrate an upload. Good to know Each wallet has its own encrypted backup file, using the password you just chose. Recently Deleted wallets are excluded. Restore these files individually. Your app passcode does not replace the backup password.

articles.title: Back up one wallet to iCloud
articles.summary: Create an encrypted recovery file for a particular wallet.
articles.body: Backup & recovery Back up one wallet to iCloud Create an encrypted recovery file for a particular wallet. Oath 4.0.3 Where to find it Settings → Wallets → wallet → Back Up to iCloud How to do it Open the wallet’s settings and turn on Back Up to iCloud. Enter and confirm a backup password with at least eight characters. Tap Back Up, then wait for the upload status to complete. Keep the password safe; the app cannot recover a forgotten backup password. Select the wallet by name before enabling its backup. A backup for one wallet is not automatically a backup for every other wallet in the app. Keep Oath open until its upload status completes. If iCloud is unavailable, fix the account, Drive, storage or connectivity issue and retry. Treat the backup as usable only when the relevant operation has completed and you retain the correct recovery material or file password. Loading, preparing and unavailable states are not successful backups. Follow along in Oath Real app screens with illustrative demo data. No live funds were sent, swapped or revoked for these examples. Never send funds to an example address. Tap an image to inspect it at full size. 1 This simulator has no iCloud account, so it shows the real unavailable state. This is not a completed backup; use an eligible signed-in device to upload. See step 1 . 2 Set and confirm the password for the encrypted backup. Empty fields are shown deliberately; the screenshot does not demonstrate an upload. Good to know Files are stored in iCloud Drive → Oath Wallet → Wallet Backups. Turning off the switch keeps existing files in iCloud Drive.

articles.title: Understand your backup password
articles.summary: The password for an iCloud backup is separate from your app passcode and BIP-39 passphrase.
articles.body: Backup & recovery Understand your backup password The password for an iCloud backup is separate from your app passcode and BIP-39 passphrase. Oath 4.0.3 Where to find it Back Up to iCloud → Encrypt Your Backup How to do it Choose a password of at least eight characters that you can recover independently. Enter it twice and use the eye controls to review the fields privately. Use that password when restoring the corresponding backup file. If you create another backup with a different password, retain the correct password for each file you keep. Choose a backup password you can recover without access to this phone. It is separate from the six-digit app passcode. Oath cannot decrypt an existing file with a newly chosen password. Keep the password that was used for each backup file you retain. Treat the backup as usable only when the relevant operation has completed and you retain the correct recovery material or file password. Loading, preparing and unavailable states are not successful backups. Follow along in Oath Real app screens with illustrative demo data. No live funds were sent, swapped or revoked for these examples. Never send funds to an example address. Tap an image to inspect it at full size. 1 This simulator has no iCloud account, so it shows the real unavailable state. This is not a completed backup; use an eligible signed-in device to upload. See step 1 . 2 Set and confirm the password for the encrypted backup. Empty fields are shown deliberately; the screenshot does not demonstrate an upload. Good to know Oath cannot reset the password of an encrypted backup. If you still have an accessible wallet, create a new backup with a password you know.

articles.title: Restore from an iCloud backup
articles.summary: Recover a wallet from an encrypted Oath backup file.
articles.body: Backup & recovery Restore from an iCloud backup Recover a wallet from an encrypted Oath backup file. Oath 4.0.3 Where to find it Welcome → more options → Restore from iCloud How to do it Sign in to the Apple Account that holds the backup and enable iCloud Drive. Choose Restore from iCloud under Welcome’s more options, in Home’s wallet-name capsule switcher, or under Settings → Wallets. Select a backup by its displayed date and enter that file’s backup password. Wait while Oath downloads, decrypts and saves the wallet. Finish customization when shown. Restoring downloads an encrypted file and requires its own backup password. Signing into the correct Apple Account alone is not sufficient to decrypt it. After restoration, compare the wallet name and public addresses with the original. Network balances and transaction history are fetched separately; allow refresh to finish. Treat the backup as usable only when the relevant operation has completed and you retain the correct recovery material or file password. Loading, preparing and unavailable states are not successful backups. Follow along in Oath Real app screens with illustrative demo data. No live funds were sent, swapped or revoked for these examples. Never send funds to an example address. Tap an image to inspect it at full size. 1 A device without an available iCloud account cannot list and restore backups. Check all wallets before deleting any local copy on the old phone. Treat the backup as usable only when the relevant operation has completed and you retain the correct recovery material or file password. If automatic biometric authentication is canceled, use the keypad or the biometric icon. If a passcode is incorrect, the dots turn red with an inline error. Try again carefully. If Oath asks you to wait after repeated failures, wait before another attempt. An incorrect code produces an inline message and red passcode dots, with a shake and error haptic where device settings allow them. There is no incorrect-passcode dialog to dismiss; wait for the entry to reset and try again. Reduce Motion can suppress the shake. Haptic feedback depends on the device and system settings; the visible error remains available. The keypad keeps its normal appearance while a biometric prompt is active. Complete or dismiss that prompt before continuing with a passcode. Authentication is still required even when the keys do not look dimmed. Follow along in Oath Real app screens with illustrative demo data. No live funds were sent, swapped or revoked for these examples. Never send funds to an example address. articles.summary: Require authentication to enter Oath.
articles.body: Security & privacy Enable passcode protection Require authentication to enter Oath. Oath 4.0.3 Where to find it Settings → Passcode & Face ID How to do it Open Passcode & Face ID. Authenticate if security is already enabled. Turn on Passcode. Enter a new six-digit code and repeat it on Confirm Passcode. If biometrics are available, complete the automatic biometric prompt to enable them as well. Review the resulting security setting before leaving. Public account activity remains visible on-chain even when the app is locked or its balance display is hidden. The passcode is six digits and protects local access to Oath. It does not replace an offline recovery phrase, imported private key or encrypted backup. If the confirmation does not match, re-enter the intended code carefully. Once setup finishes, verify that Passcode is enabled before leaving security settings. Follow along in Oath Real app screens with illustrative demo data. No live funds were sent, swapped or revoked for these examples. Never send funds to an example address. Tap an image to inspect it at full size. 1 Enter and confirm your own app passcode privately. articles.summary: Replace your Oath unlock code without changing your wallet addresses.
articles.body: Security & privacy Change your app passcode Replace your Oath unlock code without changing your wallet addresses. Enter the new six-digit passcode. Confirm it by entering the same digits again. Review the resulting security setting before leaving. Public account activity remains visible on-chain even when the app is locked or its balance display is hidden. Verifying the current passcode establishes authority to change local protection. The new code does not alter blockchain addresses or change the password of a previously uploaded backup file. If you cancel or the change fails, do not assume the new code was saved. Follow the visible result and keep the current recovery material safe. Follow along in Oath Real app screens with illustrative demo data. No live funds were sent, swapped or revoked for these examples. Never send funds to an example address. Tap an image to inspect it at full size. 1 Enter and confirm your own app passcode privately. Complete the biometric prompt. Oath enables the option after successful authentication. Keep your app passcode available for fallback access. Face ID or Touch ID is a convenience for the protected local vault. The app passcode remains the fallback when biometric authentication is unavailable or canceled. Changes to device biometrics or secure credentials can require renewed authorization. Check the resulting switch rather than assuming the system prompt succeeded. Review the resulting security setting before leaving. Public account activity remains visible on-chain even when the app is locked or its balance display is hidden. To turn off the app passcode, switch off Passcode and complete the required verification and confirmation. Review the resulting switches before leaving. Review the resulting security setting before leaving. Public account activity remains visible on-chain even when the app is locked or its balance display is hidden. Turning off biometrics alone leaves app-passcode protection available. Turning off the passcode changes the local protection policy and requires the corresponding confirmation. Use App Switcher Privacy and Hide Balances independently where appropriate. Neither is a replacement for authentication or an independent recovery backup. Follow along in Oath Real app screens with illustrative demo data. No live funds were sent, swapped or revoked for these examples. Never send funds to an example address. articles.title: Choose when Oath locks
articles.summary: Control how long Oath stays unlocked after moving to the background.

Select Immediately, 1 minute, 5 minutes or 10 minutes. Return to the security screen to see the saved selection. Review the resulting security setting before leaving. Choose Immediately for the shortest grace period. Restarting the app requires authentication when passcode protection is enabled. The delay is not a promise that signing or sensitive settings will skip their own confirmation. Follow along in Oath Real app screens with illustrative demo data. No live funds were sent, swapped or revoked for these examples. Never send funds to an example address. Tap an image to inspect it at full size. 1 Security settings group passcode, biometric, locking and app-switcher privacy controls. No authentication secret is shown. articles.summary: End the current unlocked session without waiting for the automatic delay.
articles.body: Security & privacy Lock Oath immediately End the current unlocked session without waiting for the automatic delay. Oath 4.0.3 Where to find it Settings → lock icon How to do it Open Settings from Home. Tap the lock icon in the top bar. Oath presents the unlock screen. articles.title: What if I forget my app passcode?
articles.summary: Keep recovery options separate from the app lock.
articles.body: Security & privacy What if I forget my app passcode? Keep recovery options separate from the app lock. Oath 4.0.3 Where to find it Unlock screen How to do it If biometric unlock still works, use it to access the app and make sure your recovery backups are available. Locate your recovery phrase, private key or encrypted iCloud backup and its password. Include the BIP-39 passphrase for any passphrase wallet. Do not delete Oath until you have verified a usable recovery route. If needed, ask support for guidance without sending any secret recovery material. Oath support cannot tell you your passcode or reconstruct a missing recovery phrase. Resetting the app is not a way to bypass decryption of the existing vault. Do not remove the app or its final wallet while it holds your only usable recovery copy. Preserve the device and seek guidance using nonsecret information. Review the resulting security setting before leaving. Public account activity remains visible on-chain even when the app is locked or its balance display is hidden. articles.title: Reset Oath on this device
articles.summary: Erase local app data and return to setup.
articles.body: Security & privacy Reset Oath on this device Erase local app data and return to setup. Oath 4.0.3 Where to find it Settings → Reset App How to do it Confirm you can recover every wallet you want to keep before starting. Open Reset App at the bottom of Settings. Complete authentication when requested. Read the reset warning and confirm only if you intend to erase the local installation’s data. Review the resulting security setting before leaving. Public account activity remains visible on-chain even when the app is locked or its balance display is hidden. Reset removes local wallets and associated app data and returns the installation to Welcome. It cannot reverse transfers, erase public chain history or revoke on-chain allowances. An encrypted iCloud backup is a separate file. Keep its original password and any other required recovery information if you want to restore afterward. If you only want to remove one wallet while keeping others, use Wallets instead. The last-wallet removal has its own Recently Deleted confirmation sequence. articles.title: Find and add a token by address
articles.summary: Look up a supported contract or mint address and review its details before adding it.
articles.body: Assets & networks Find and add a token by address Look up a supported contract or mint address and review its details before adding it. Oath 4.0.3 Where to find it Bottom navigation → Wallet → Search → token address How to do it Tap Wallet, then the magnifying-glass Search icon. Paste the exact token contract address, or Solana mint address. Wait for lookup on supported networks present in the active wallet. If some lookups fail, use Try Again for an incomplete result. Tap a result and review its network, full address, name, symbol, standard and decimals. Compare the full token identity with information you obtained independently from the project, then tap Add Token. After addition succeeds, tap the native checkmark to finish. Oath tracks the token for that account. Manual lookup is available for the supported EVM networks, TRON and Solana. The same-looking address or symbol on a different network is a different token. articles.title: Why does my address need funds to activate?
articles.summary: Understand account activation, minimum balances and storage on Stellar, XRP Ledger, Solana, TRON, NEAR and Gram (TON). Oath does not charge an activation fee.
articles.body: Send & receive Why does my address need funds to activate? Understand account activation, minimum balances and storage on Stellar, XRP Ledger, Solana, TRON, NEAR and Gram (TON). Oath does not charge an activation fee. Oath 4.0.3 Where to find it Home → Receive → choose an asset → activation notice → Learn more… How to do it Choose the wallet you want to receive into, open Receive and select the correct asset and network. If an activation notice appears below the address, read its network and amount. It concerns this address on this network, not every wallet in Oath. Use the address shown in Receive to fund your own account on that same network. Follow the relevant network section below; sending a token may not activate the native account. Check the sender’s review before confirming. Allow for any sender fee or exchange withdrawal fee so the amount actually received meets the requirement. After the transfer confirms, reopen Receive to check again. On Gram (TON), funding and deploying the wallet contract are separate steps, so funding alone can leave a deployment notice. Why a new address can need funding Creating or importing a wallet gives you an address before that address necessarily exists as an account on the blockchain. Some networks require a reserve, some require funds for storage, and some deploy a wallet contract. These rules help limit spam and pay for maintaining or processing on-chain data. They are network rules, not an Oath subscription. Oath does not charge or collect an activation fee. Fund the receiving address in your own wallet, not an address supplied by someone claiming to activate it for you. Network transaction fees, network account-creation charges, storage costs and an exchange’s withdrawal fees can still apply. Oath cannot waive these charges or change a network’s reserve. A reserve or storage deposit is different from a fee: it may stay in an account while being unavailable to spend. A network fee is consumed under that network’s rules. Do not assume that every amount called activation is refundable. Stellar (XLM): a minimum account balance An ordinary new Stellar account needs two base reserves. At the time of this update, one base reserve is 0.5 XLM, so a basic account needs 1 XLM. Oath reads the current ledger reserve for its notice. The sender must use a transfer flow that creates a new Stellar account; an ordinary payment to a nonexistent account is not enough. The reserve remains in your Stellar account; Oath does not receive it. It normally cannot be spent while the account requires it. Trustlines and other ledger entries can increase the minimum, commonly by another base reserve each. For example, holding an issued token can require a trustline in addition to activation. Sponsored reserves can change who supplies the balance. Keep extra XLM available for transaction fees; sending an issued token alone does not create an ordinary new account. Source: https://developers.stellar.org/docs/learn/fundamentals/lumens XRP Ledger (XRP): the base reserve A new XRP Ledger address becomes an account when it receives enough XRP to meet the base reserve. The published Mainnet base reserve is currently 1 XRP; Oath uses the validated ledger’s current value. Additional owned objects can raise the reserve, currently generally 0.2 XRP per item, with exceptions and sponsorship rules. Reserved XRP stays in the account and is normally unavailable for ordinary payments. It is not paid to Oath. Network transaction costs are separate and can consume XRP even below the reserve. Qualifying account deletion can recover part of a reserve, but has its own network rules and cost; removing a wallet from Oath does not delete its on-chain account. Activate with XRP first, not an issued token. An already existing account can receive smaller XRP payments. Source: https://xrpl.org/docs/concepts/accounts/reserves Solana (SOL): account funding and token-account deposits Solana accounts need enough SOL for their rent-exempt balance, which depends on the space they use. For an address that does not yet have a native account, Oath asks the network for the current minimum for a basic account rather than assuming every account needs the same amount. The SOL remains in that account; it is not an Oath activation payment. Keep additional SOL for future transaction fees. USDC, USDT and other Solana tokens live in separate token accounts. A sender can create the required token account and fund its deposit while transferring a token, even if the wallet owner has no SOL balance. Receiving tokens therefore does not prove the owner’s native SOL account is funded. A token-account deposit is separate from the transaction fee; eligible token accounts can be closed to reclaim their remaining SOL under the token program’s rules. Account size and token extensions can change the deposit. Source: https://solana.com/docs/core/accounts/account-structure Source: https://solana.com/docs/tokens/basics/create-token-account Source: https://solana.com/docs/tokens/basics/close-account TRON (TRX): account creation paid by the sender A newly generated TRON address is activated by receiving TRX or a TRC-10 transfer from an existing account, or by an account-creation operation. Receiving only a TRC-20 token such as USDT does not perform that native-account activation. For standard activation, the sender pays the network account-creation charge: currently 1 TRX, plus a possible 0.1 TRX creation Bandwidth charge when staked or delegated Bandwidth is insufficient. Parameters can change. Contract-based activation follows different Energy and Bandwidth rules. These are consumed network charges, not a minimum TRX balance held by the recipient and not an Oath fee. The amount sent to the recipient remains theirs. After activation, TRX or sufficient network resources are still needed to send, especially for TRC-20 tokens. A token transfer’s cost is not fixed by this activation example. Source: https://developers.tron.network/docs/account NEAR: creating an implicit account and covering storage Oath’s generated NEAR address is a 64-character implicit account ID. A native NEAR transfer creates that account on chain and credits the transferred balance. The warning applies to this implicit-address flow; it is not a way to register an arbitrary missing name ending in .near. Keep enough NEAR for the account’s storage requirements and later transaction fees. Storage usage, account configuration and token-contract registration can affect the required amount, so this guide does not promise one universal activation deposit. NEAR reserved for storage is unavailable for other uses while that storage is required. Token registration can require a separate storage deposit with a token contract, and sending a token does not substitute for creating the native account. Oath does not collect these balances. Any storage refund depends on the account or contract’s supported rules; deleting the wallet in the app does not refund on-chain storage. Source: https://github.com/near/nearcore/blob/master/docs/DataStructures/Account.md Source: https://docs.near.org/protocol/storage/storage-staking Gram (TON): fund, then deploy the wallet contract Oath displays this network as Gram and its native coin as GRAM. TON wallets are smart contracts. A new address can first receive funds while its contract is still uninitialized. The initial native-coin transfer should be non-bounceable; use the receiving address supplied by Oath and a sender that supports this network. Funding the address and deploying the contract are different steps. Oath includes the wallet’s deployment data with its first outgoing transaction when required. Until the contract is active, the notice can remain even when the balance is positive. You do not need to repeatedly deposit just because deployment is still pending. There is no single fixed deposit that guarantees every deployment or transfer. Keep enough native coin for the estimated deployment, transaction and storage costs. The unused balance remains in your account; actual network charges are consumed. Jettons such as USDT do not replace native coin for these costs. Oath does not take an activation fee. Source: https://docs.ton.org/foundations/status Source: https://docs.ton.org/foundations/fees What about the other supported networks? Oath does not show this account-activation notice for ordinary wallet receipts on Bitcoin-family networks, EVM networks, Sui, Aptos or THORChain. This does not mean transactions are free. Sender fees, minimum transfer or dust rules, token-specific requirements and funds needed for a later outgoing transaction are different questions. Why the notice appears, disappears or stays visible Oath checks the selected receiving address in the background. It shows this notice only when the network check confirms an absent or undeployed account. It does not block copying or sharing the address. An account already reported active does not get this activation notice, even if it later needs more funds for fees or other reserves. A failed or unavailable network check is not proof that an account is inactive, so Oath does not show an activation warning for an unknown result. The absence of this notice is therefore not a guarantee that a transfer will succeed. Check the correct network, address, amount and sender review. Each address and network has its own state; activating one does not activate all your wallets. Good to know Network values can change. Use the current amount shown in Oath and review the sender’s charges. Never share recovery words, a passphrase or a private key to activate an account. Oath does not charge an activation fee; network costs and third-party withdrawal fees may still apply.

articles.title: Understand pending, confirmed and failed activity
articles.summary: Use status to distinguish a submitted transaction from a settled one.
articles.body: Transactions & activity Understand pending, confirmed and failed activity Use status to distinguish a submitted transaction from a settled one.
